bullets.title: Nasdaq/semis slammed as AI/memory stocks lead tech lower
bullets.body: US equities closed mixed-to-weak: S&P 500 -0.28-0.3%, Nasdaq -0.6-0.76%, Dow +0.1-0.26%. Semiconductors were the worst performer, down 2.7-3.7%, with momentum stocks broadly under pressure. Equal-weight S&P +0.2% showed the divergence — strength in Industrials (+10x overbought closes vs oversold), REITs, and Utilities offset tech weakness.

bullets.title: NVDA down 7 straight days ahead of pivotal Wed earnings; JPM and StreetAccount preview beat-and-raise
bullets.body: NVDA enters earnings on a 7-day losing streak with stock up 70% since the AI watch party. JPM's Spec Sales desk expects Q2 revenue ~$94-95B and a Q3 guide of $107-108B, well above buyside bars, with material short covering and stock at 10-year valuation lows. StreetAccount consensus sits at $92.3B Q2 revenue and $104.2B Q3 guide; options imply a 4.6-6.1% move. Gross margins expected to hold at 75%.

bullets.title: NVDA price hikes hitting hyperscalers as memory costs soar; MU/SNDK take collateral damage
bullets.body: Nvidia is informing hyperscalers of 15%+ price hikes on systems shipped next year due to soaring memory costs. Micron fell 5.8% and SNDK declined ~5-6% as the market views memory inflation as the proximate trigger. Amazon separately hiking memory prices 60%. Early Blackwell/Vera Rubin buyers before Jan 31, 2027 benefit from locked-in pricing ahead of hikes.

bullets.title: NVDA unveils Vera Rubin metrics: 30x throughput/watt vs GB300, 35x lower token cost for agentic AI
bullets.body: First on-silicon performance data for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 shows 30x more throughput per megawatt and 35x lower token cost vs the GB300 NVL72, measured specifically for agentic workloads. Groq 3 LPX entered full production at 3,400 tokens/sec. SpaceX AI adopted the Vera CPU for agentic AI orchestration; Nebius was first AI cloud to adopt Groq 3 LPX.

bullets.title: Treasury bond buybacks expand but Wolfe, JPM, and Citadel skeptical of yield-suppression efficacy
bullets.body: Treasury announced increasing buyback sizes from $2B to at least $4B per operation for longer-dated Treasuries, with reports that the $935B-$1T TGA could fund purchases rather than T-bill issuance. Gold rallied and the yield curve flattened on the news. However, Wolfe Research estimates the current run-rate of $72B/year would need to scale 8x to match Fed's Operation Twist (15-20bp impact), and Citadel called it 'financial repression' risking dollar weakness. Bessent confirmed no bonds purchased yet; next operation Sept. 9.

bullets.title: Gold hits 3-month high above $4,700 on debasement trade; record speculative long positioning
bullets.body: Gold futures extended gains above $4,700/oz, up 16% over the past month, as the Treasury's TGA-drain-for-buybacks narrative revived debasement concerns. Speculative net long positions surged a record $22.2B — the largest increase in over a decade. Japan's 10-year yield also hit a 28-year high above 2.95%, adding to global fixed income stress.

bullets.title: Trump escalates Canada trade war: 50% tariffs on autos, parts, steel from Jan 1, 2027
bullets.body: Trump posted on Truth Social announcing 50% tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel effective January 1, 2027, with zero tariffs for goods built in the US. US-Canada deal collapsed Friday; Canada's retaliatory tariffs delayed to Sept. 8. Ontario Premier Ford threatened to cut electricity and critical minerals exports to the US. VP Vance confirmed negotiations are ongoing but accused Canada of last-minute unreasonable demands.

bullets.title: Trump eyes 7.5% additional tariff on China over excess capacity, ahead of Sept 24 Xi meeting
bullets.body: The US is considering imposing a new 7.5% overcapacity tariff on Chinese goods, which would raise the total Trump second-term baseline tariff on China to ~20%. Timing is one month before the September 24 Trump-Xi meeting. White House initially said non-official tariff news is 'just speculation.'

bullets.title: Bessent's 'Economic D-Day' Iran sanctions: zero-leakage approach, major financial institution sanction imminent
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent unveiled sweeping Iran sanctions: nearly 60 entities/people/vessels targeted across nuclear, missile, cyber, and oil networks. Secondary sanctions now cover five sectors (digital assets, tech, gold, aviation, shipping). Every country has a defined timeline to close Iran-linked banking; Bessent warned that any country helping Iran faces removal from the dollar system. He expects a major financial institution to be sanctioned by week's end. China specifically warned.

bullets.title: Bessent signals limited bond-market resolve; Wolfe says Iran sanctions more warning than enforcement
bullets.body: Wolfe DC Policy notes Bessent declined to project 'whatever it takes' resolve on bond intervention and the Iranian 'Economic D-Day' rollout largely targeted already-sanctioned entities. Bessent explicitly stated he won't impose secondary sanctions that would 'blow up the global financial system,' making China sanctions over Iran unlikely. FT compared Bessent's bond strategy to geopolitical overreach with no clear path to victory.

bullets.title: US crude at 50-year inventory low; oil falls 1-2% on Iran sanctions anticipation
bullets.body: US crude oil inventory fell to 41 days of supply — the lowest in 50 years — and SPR dropped another 3.7M barrels to 289.7M, the lowest since 1982. Despite tight physical supply, WTI fell ~1.8% to $85.51 and Brent dropped 1.2% to $93.23 as traders anticipated Iran sanctions. Distillate inventories are also at the lowest level since 1996. Shipping through Strait of Hormuz now costs ~$20M per supertanker per TotalEnergies CEO.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole week: Warsh speech unlikely to deliver clear rate signal; focus on inflation control
bullets.body: Stifel expects Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech to emphasize commitment to inflation control without providing clear rate direction. JPM is tactically bullish but with lower conviction ahead of both NVDA earnings and the Warsh speech; a double disappointment could trigger a 3-4% SPX pullback. The rise in US yields since Warsh's first FOMC meeting has been driven primarily by higher term premium, not rate expectations.

bullets.title: Chicago Fed activity index turns slightly negative in July; consumer confidence weak
bullets.body: Chicago Fed National Activity Index came in at -0.08 in July vs. -0.09 expected (down from +0.06 in June), signaling growth slightly below historical trend. Only 8% of consumers expect income growth to outpace inflation over the next year per University of Michigan survey, a notable negative for consumer-facing names.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle: cumulative spend approaching $3T by year-end; surpasses oil & gas in 2026
bullets.body: AI capex projected to reach $765B in 2026, surpassing oil and gas spending for the first time ever. Cumulative lifetime AI capex expected to approach $3T by year-end, driving record debt issuance. Hyperscalers have lined up $2.6T in planned future spend. Token consumption accelerating 45% m/m in August per RJ Token Observer. 22V flags that enormous AI financing needs may keep upward pressure on yields and slow (but ultimately extend) the AI investment cycle.

bullets.title: Macro managers turning bearish on USD; stock-bond correlation shifting toward 'fire' regime
bullets.body: Macro managers are adopting bearish USD stances in response to Fed and Treasury policy shifts. A separate academic framework note argues the stock-bond correlation has shifted from 'ice' (bonds hedge equity) to 'fire' (bonds no longer reliably hedge equities), and that markets now require fiscal consolidation signals — rising term premium will continue until consolidation is forced.

bullets.title: China dumps $60B in US Treasuries since February amid trade tension escalation
bullets.body: China has sold $60B in US Treasuries since February, signaling a strategic shift away from US debt holdings. German Finance Minister attributed the broader global bond yield surge to Trump's trade war. 30-year Treasury yield is emerging as the market's primary fear gauge, with 66% of Bloomberg survey respondents expecting the 10-year to exceed 5%.

bullets.title: NVIDIA deepens AI factory ecosystem: Lancium strategic investment, SpaceX partnership, $6B open-source bet
bullets.body: NVIDIA made a strategic investment in Lancium (a Blackstone portfolio company) to deploy its full-stack AI factory platform across a 15+ GW pipeline. SpaceX AI adopted the Vera CPU for agentic workloads and is scaling Grok on the Vera Rubin platform; a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 targets orbital launch by Q4 2027 with significant scale in 2028. NVIDIA is also reportedly committing $6B to open-source AI initiatives.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: Industrials most overbought, Energy/Tech lead YTD but most volatile; REITs outperform
bullets.body: Industrials closed at short-term overbought levels 10x more than oversold — the highest ratio among all sectors. Energy and Technology are the top two YTD performers but also have the most frequent worst-day occurrences. S&P 500 RE Index +0.59% vs S&P 500 -0.28% on the session, with office REITs +1.96% and Data Center REITs down 1.01% on the day despite being +31% YTD.

bullets.title: US housing demand hits record low; 80% of major metros now buyer's markets
bullets.body: US homebuyer demand fell to a record low with 967,000 buyers competing against 1.46 million sellers — a 51% seller surplus. Per Redfin data, 80% of major metros are now classified as buyer's markets. Existing home prices and mortgage rates remain materially elevated vs. 10 years ago (30yr rate was 3.4%, median price $243K).

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO filing imminent; Poolside raises $1B from NVIDIA; OpenAI targets 2027 IPO
bullets.body: Anthropic is set to file for IPO as early as end of August, expecting to meet or exceed SpaceX's record IPO size (General Atlantic working with JPM, MS, GS). Poolside raised $1B from NVIDIA. OpenAI CFO signals public offering in 2027 or sooner. Separately, Aggreko Inc. filed for NYSE IPO under ticker AGKO with Goldman, JPM, BofA, Barclays, Morgan Stanley as book-runners.
